national.title: Oil prices inch back up as Iran and the Houthis escalate threats
national.summary: Increased fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia and Tehran's unrelenting threats in the Strait of Hormuz appear to be reversing weeks of oil price declines.
national.body: Ship transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen again this month and the amount of crude oil and other products shipped outside the Persian Gulf remains at just over half of pre-war levels, according to data from shipping intelligence company Kpler. The number of ships making the journey per week fell from 217 to 147 between Nov. 1 and Nov. 23, Kpler said in two reports this week. Tanker crossings averaged 11 per day for the week ending Nov. 21, compared to 50 per day before the war, meanwhile, though the company noted that many crossings are "dark," or done with their AIS transmission systems turned off, usually for safety reasons. The International Maritime Organization has recorded 141 attacks on commercial ships in and around the strait since the war began in February, including at least 15 in November. October was the worst month for attacks on vessels in the region since the war began, with at least 35 ships coming under attack according to the IMO.

national.summary: Text of the treaties will be published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.
national.body:
Economics editor Published 26 November 2026, 02:13 GMT Updated 21 minutes ago The government and the EU are set to publish the texts of two treaties that were agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.

The treaties will be published on Thursday afternoon, alongside legislation which is designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

The BBC understands the deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the new deal.

Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would scrap the deal and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has suggested he would refuse to pay.

The Brexit reset deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, its costs, and a wider discussion on the long-term UK-EU relationship.

The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

Two of the three legal texts will be released on Thursday, covering the food trade and emissions trading scheme deals, alongside the government's cost-cutting bill to enact the deal.

New assessments of the impact of the deal on different sectors and regions of the country are also expected.

national.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
national.summary: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.
national.body:
US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.

The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, would "support America's booming super intelligence economy".

However, rival firm Amazon has criticised it as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan", while astronomers in the US said the move would "significantly undermine" the public's ability to study and observe the night sky.

There is increasing opposition to data centres on earth, including in the US where experts say they were a factor in the Republicans big losses in the midterm elections.

SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth".

"This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said.

national.title: Two screenings of Pakistani TV show cancelled in India after backlash
national.summary: The show, Dar-e-Nijaat, has become a sensation in India but is now embroiled in a political row.
national.body:
Until Wednesday, the weekend plans of some television enthusiasts in the Indian city of Bengaluru involved dressing up, having an elaborate dinner and finding out what happens next in the lives of a wildly popular fictional Pakistani couple.

Two private screenings of Dar-e-Nijaat (Door to Salvation), a Pakistani television drama that has become something of a sensation on Indian social media, were called off after an online backlash and police scrutiny.

The serial, which airs on Pakistan's ARY Digital, is available to Indian viewers through some YouTube channels, though the broadcaster's official channel is blocked in India.

The controversy comes amid a renewed appetite for Pakistani entertainment in India, even though cultural engagement remains a sensitive issue following a brief but intense military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed neighbours in May last year.

A similar gathering in Delhi, featuring quizzes and even a virtual interaction with the show's director, had already divided opinion online last week.

In Bengaluru, one screening, scheduled for Saturday at a restaurant, offered a Persian and Arabic dinner alongside two episodes of the serial for a small ticket charge. The other - scheduled at a private theatre and meant only for family members - asked guests to dress in their "best Pakistani ensemble".

As promotional posters circulated online, several social media users questioned the appropriateness of such gatherings and called for police intervention. Both events have since been called off.

The backlash has coincided with calls to block the release of another Pakistani drama in India.

national.title: Four-time MVP Rodgers released and may have played last NFL game
national.summary: Aaron Rodgers is replaced as the Pittsburgh Steelers' starting quarterback, then criticises head coach Mike McCarthy before being released with immediate effect.
national.body:
Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In a brief statement published on Wednesday afternoon local time, the Steelers announced Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, was no longer with the franchise.

That came after a tumultuous 24 hours, which began with the Steelers announcing at 23:10 local time on Tuesday that Rodgers had been replaced as their starting quarterback.

He then appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, saying he would not rejoin the team.

"That ship has sailed," said Rodgers, who turns 43 next week.

During the 34-minute interview, he said he discovered he had been replaced from team-mate Pat Freiermuth.

Rodgers was also critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings.

They won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2011 and, during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers said that McCarthy ended the half-time huddle with a chant of "one, two, three, Packers".

national.title: Guinea orders residents to clean up the capital months after deadly rubbish dump collapse
national.summary: The capital's main rubbish dump has been closed since the disaster, leading to rubbish piling up in the streets.
national.body:
Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday announced a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.

In August heavy rains caused a landslide at the capital's main waste dump, with the rubbish collapsing onto homes killing 31 people and injuring others.

The site in the city's Dar es Salaam area was subsequently closed permanently, which has led to piles of rubbish accumulating outside homes and on the streets.

At a public forum on sanitation, Sanitation Minister Aboubacar Camara said Conakry was generating about 3,000 tonnes of waste every day.

He said much of the garbage was ending up in the streets because of weaknesses in the collection system.

The prime minister called on local authorities to become more involved in organising waste collection, saying this could become a way to create jobs.

"The state will do its part, but the municipalities must also organise themselves to ensure waste collection and provide jobs for young people," the prime minister said.

national.title: FedEx plane overshoots Miami runway, causing brief suspension of flights at airport
national.summary: The brief stoppage came on the eve of the US Thanksgiving holiday, one of the busiest travel days of the year.
national.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) temporarily halted flights bound for Miami International Airport in Florida after a FedEx aircraft overran a runway on Wednesday evening.

Departures heading to Miami were grounded just after 20:15 local time (01:15 GMT) and all but one runway at the airport was closed, according to the FAA advisory. Flights resumed again about 90 minutes later.

The airliner that ran past the runway arrived from Memphis. No injuries have been reported. The FAA is investigating the incident.

The ground stop came on the day before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest travel days of the year in the US.

Flight delays in Miami reached one hour but appeared to be declining later Wednesday night.

At 21:41 local time, the FAA confirmed that "flights will be resuming shortly".

Passengers scheduled to travel on Wednesday night were encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight updates before heading to the airport.

"We appreciate our passengers' patience as we work to safely resume normal operations," Miami-Dade Aviation Department spokesman Greg Chin said in a statement to the BBC.

national.title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold
national.summary: Indonesian authorities say another 13 are missing in the illegal gold mine, which flooded on Monday.
national.body:
It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday. Early on Tuesday, she received news that he was trapped underground.

Rais, 50, had been working as an illegal gold miner in Bogor, Indonesia's West Java province. On Monday night, he and at least 25 other miners were digging in an open-pit mine about 100m (328ft) deep, when torrential rain caused a nearby river to overflow and flood the two shafts.

Authorities on Thursday confirmed that 13 people had died and their bodies were recovered from the site. At least 13 more are thought to still be missing.

Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing, with personnel using ropes to access the depths of the dark, narrow and slippery mine shafts, which are continually being flooded from below.

Above ground, ambulances and medical personnel are ready and waiting to transport victims.

"We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft," Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting are key considerations in determining the search strategy so that personnel can operate safely."

Small-scale gold mining is banned in Indonesia, but remains widespread in rural parts of the mineral-rich archipelago.

national.title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats
national.summary: Gen Kainerugaba threatened a rebel takeover of a mineral-rich area in DR Congo in controversial X posts.
national.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.

In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo. He insisted that Uganda's military involvement was purely driven by security concerns.

The DR Congo's foreign ministry summoned Uganda's envoy to explain the remarks, describing them as "particularly serious" and damaging to diplomatic relations.

The diplomatic row comes despite close military ties between the neighbours.

Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DR Congo since 2021.

Uganda has also recently been involved in efforts to mediate between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.

national.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
national.summary: The Trump administration gave Elon Musk's SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a move that has raised skepticism among scientists.
national.body:
FILE - Elon Musk listens as President Donald Trump speaks during an event at the U.S. Institute of Peace, Oct. 8, 2026, in Washington. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption

The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

Big tech's next move is to put data centers in space. Can it work? The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX's one million "orbital compute modules" (forming a data center constellation called "Starmind") would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing "the full power of the sun."

"America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was appointed by Republican President Donald Trump, said in a statement. He added that Wednesday's move "opens a bold new frontier."

A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least "one authorized space station" by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040. Musk welcomed the decision over social media.

The world's richest man has long vowed to form vast, solar-powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth. But scientists and industry experts have stressed enormous technical and financial obstacles, as well as a host of environmental concerns.

Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and author, called the prospect of launching a million satellites into space to create data centers "a fantasy."

Technology Google launches Project Suncatcher, a step towards AI data centers in space Proponents of data centers in space argue that capturing the sun's energy would ease pressure on power grids and cut demand for sprawling computing warehouses on Earth (and resources like water needed to cool them). Space seems to offer a solution because it is cold, but it is also a vacuum, trapping heat inside objects much like a thermos. Becker explained that there are "basic physical limits" to otherwise radiating that heat out — and sending lots of smaller satellites could potentially carry the necessary material combined, but it would be expensive and difficult.

national.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
national.summary: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".
national.body:
FILE - Music group Duran Duran poses at The Sony Club in New York, Oct. 12, 2004. From left are John Taylor, Nick Rhodes, Roger Taylor, Simon Le Bon and Andy Taylor. Jim Cooper/AP hide caption

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed," the band said.

FILE - Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor listens as a fellow band member answers a question at a news conference in Hong Kong, Aug. 26, 2004. Lo Sai-hung/AP hide caption

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."

The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

national.title: Steelers cut Aaron Rodgers after the QB rips coach Mike McCarthy on TV
national.summary: The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday's visit from Denver.
national.body:
FILE - Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, left, and Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, right, stand together during the second half of an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Pittsburgh, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. Gene J. Puskar/AP hide caption

The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time MVP on Wednesday, shortly after he torched Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show."

The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday's visit from Denver.

Rodgers responded by taking an excused absence from the club, then used the unexpected time off to go on McAfee's show and repeatedly call out the 62-year-old McCarthy's mental fitness. Rodgers told McAfee he found out about the surprise decision to bench him while on the phone with teammates, including tight end Pat Freiermuth.

McCarthy said later Wednesday, after Rodgers was released, that there were "continuous efforts" to reach the player he's known for two decades dating to their time together in Green Bay.

While McCarthy declined to get into personal conversations, he said things came to a head Tuesday when Rodgers offered an "ultimatum" that McCarthy felt was "clearly out of his job description."

Asked if the decision to cut Rodgers came after he went scorched earth on national television, McCarthy said he couldn't pinpoint the exact timeline because he was in and out of meetings all afternoon.

A Pittsburgh native hired in January to replace Mike Tomlin, McCarthy also brushed off Rodgers' suggestion that the coach had lost the team, saying he had a "very direct, very honest" meeting with the club's players' council after practice Wednesday and believes the Steelers will respond with the proper urgency.

national.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
national.summary: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.

In recent weeks, the 21-year-old has been unable to walk properly after her legs were beaten, and an ear-infection caused by an untreated head injury has affected her balance, her cousin says.

She is "keeping her spirits up" but "there are days she breaks down in tears," Masoud Nourmohammadi tells BBC News Persian.

He says Taraneh and her twin sister Romina were arrested after joining the anti-government protests that swept the country in January.

When the twins' mother first saw them in prison, their faces were so swollen and bruised, and their hair pulled out, that she could only recognise them by their voices, Nourmohammadi says, speaking from the US.

He says Taraneh signed a confession after interrogators threatened that her sister would be raped in front of her.

Taraneh is one of six women who have been sentenced to death this year in connection with the January protests, according to the UN's human rights rapporteur for Iran, Mai Sato.

The figure for men is much higher. However, women protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, as part of a "horrific rise" in politically motivated executions, Amnesty International's Iran researcher Raha Bahreini says.

The Iranian embassy in London told the BBC that claims of an increase in the use of the death penalty in protest-related cases were "misleading".

national.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time in history
national.summary: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
national.body: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday. The 100th annual parade will now kick off Saturday at 8:30 a.m.The historic move comes as a powerful coastal storm is set to impact the area Thursday. "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we've made the decision to move the celebration due to expected severe weather," Macy's said in a statement. "Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.""Created by Macy's colleagues since 1924 as a gift to our city and nation, our parade has brought magic into the hearts of millions and have created cherished memories that have spanned generations," Will Coss, executive producer and vice president of Macy's Branded Entertainment, said at a press conference Wednesday. "This year we marked our 100th march, a milestone built on creativity, celebration and tradition. While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our participants and spectators is and always will be our top priority." "We know that our city is the greatest city in the world, and we also know that in our city, nothing comes easily, and you have to plan for every possibility," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "And while we were looking forward to celebrating Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow, extreme weather has forced us to reschedule for Saturday instead." Mamdani pointed to the "heavy storm" expected Thursday, with wind gusts up to 65 mph possible, along with potential flash flooding. "Now I know many New Yorkers, myself included as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," Mamdani said. "I know that this change of plan will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first. And on Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting, will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe." "By moving the parade to Saturday when weather conditions are much more favorable, we can give New Yorkers the celebration that they've been looking forward to without compromising on safety," NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.New York Gov. national.summary: The musician, who co-wrote some of the band's biggest hits, had been treated for prostate cancer.
national.body:
Music correspondent Published 25 November 2026 Updated 4 hours ago Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.

Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.

In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".

His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".

Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off

Published 12 hours ago The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.

The group went on to achieve global fame through the New Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.

Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.

national.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
national.summary: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.
national.body:
A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

We confronted the 35-year-old at his business near Dortmund, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

Reuter cannot be formally charged until extradited to France but could face jail time, if tried and convicted. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The BBC - alongside German broadcasters WDR and NDR, newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) - and France's Le Monde newspaper - has obtained and reviewed hundreds of police, court and tax documents about the case. We have blurred images of Reuter because of German privacy rules.

Investigators, we have learned, believe they have uncovered clear, persistent links between Reuter and smuggling networks.

national.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
national.summary: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
national.body:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.

The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal .

China is facing the highest tariff rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%, with others facing either 20% or 25%.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed tariffs together with extensive reports of how each jurisdiction's trade practices purportedly impact American commerce.

The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and have to go through rounds of public consultation and, potentially, hearings.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of a good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing products.

Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.

national.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
national.summary: The was the first time ever that the iconic celebration was delayed because of storms. New York expects damaging winds and heavy rainfall over the Thanksgiving holiday.
national.body:
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of severe weather.

Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers, had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay.

The last time the parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never been postponed due to weather. In 1971, Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture, because of weather.

A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.

On Wednesday night, New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency for Long Island, New York City and Westchester County

The potent nor'easter is expected to make it too windy and dangerous for the iconic balloons to fly.

Macy's had expected to put 100 inflatables into the sky to mark its 100th parade and feature 10 new balloons, including one depicting the animated dog Bluey wearing a crown and another showing a Minion character riding a banana like a horse.

"While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators is, and always will be, our top priority," said Will Cross, the parade's executive producer, during a news conference on Wednesday with city officials.

national.body: A federal judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from moving forward with an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses Wednesday, a move the network argues is an attempt by the Trump administration to punish speech it does not like.In a 45-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan found ABC is likely to succeed in showing the FCC's license review was retaliatory. Her preliminary injunction bars the FCC from "taking any continuing or further action against [ABC] in relation to the early license renewal proceedings" while the network's lawsuit against the agency works its way through the courts. The judge pointed to at least 11 different examples of President Trump publicly urging the FCC to strip ABC of its licenses in recent years — an action the president argues is necessary because the network's news coverage or late-night shows are unfair to him. AliKhan also said FCC Chair Brendan Carr — who frequently echoes Mr. Trump's criticism of media outlets — "has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders.""Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face—loss of their broadcast licenses—the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," the judge wrote.She said the question of whether ABC's interest in a preliminary injunction outweighed the federal government's interests was "not a close case." national.summary: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms and flooding, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.
national.body:
Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday.

Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month.

The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.

Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US.

Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed.

Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned.

Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area.

In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft.

national.body: A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the Health Ministry. The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Warraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars."It was a huge fire; the cars got stuck together because of the fire," he told the AP, describing the fear and panic that followed. "It was a shocking scene."Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further. Initial statements said 25 people were injured, but that figure was later revised to 21.Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a massive multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

national.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died at age 65 following a battle with prostate cancer.
national.body: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran — whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" — and who were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.Taylor died following a "courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family and the band said in a joint statement posted to social media. He died Monday at his home surrounded by friends and family."To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his family said. On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend."I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."His family said Wednesday that Taylor "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination until the very end, never losing his love of life."The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients."Andy was there at the very beginning of our story," the band said in Wednesday's statement. national.title: The US pastor who wants to see women's right to vote overturned
national.summary: The movement to repeal women's right to vote has gained traction amongst some very conservative Christians.
national.body:
"Patriarchy is in accordance with the way God made the world." That is the view of Pastor Doug Wilson, a conservative minister who the US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth calls his mentor.

Speaking to the BBC from his base in Moscow, Idaho, Wilson explained his view that a society led by men is "a very great blessing". It's a perspective Christians who disagree with him say is based on a fundamentalist understanding of the Bible, which promotes the subjugation of women.

A self-described Christian nationalist, Wilson believes the US should be a theocracy, with gay sex criminalised, abortion outlawed, and people of other faiths unable to hold public office.

In the past he has delivered a sermon on "The Lost Virtue of Sexism," arguing that the Bible says women should be excluded from leadership of the church, and certain roles in civic affairs. And as part of his views on the division between the sexes, he would like the 19th Amendment of the US constitution, which granted women the right to vote, to be repealed, something his detractors say is anti-democratic.

The vast majority of Christians support women's right to vote, and dismiss his message as misogynistic and extreme.

Rev. Canon Dana Colley Corsello, the vicar at the Washington National Cathedral, rejects Wilson's understanding of what the Bible says about women's roles.

"In my mind, there is no biblical precedent or standing for what [Wilson has] proposed," she told the BBC.

"I'm married, I have a husband, I have children. My husband and I are complete equals in everything we do."

national.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
national.summary: Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.
national.body:
The US military has hailed as a "huge success" the detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa, an operation that sparked fears of health and environmental problems across the region.

Smoke was seen rising into the sky shortly after 09:00 local time (14:00 GMT) following the explosion, as the Army declared the risk "as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible".

Plans to detonate the lead azide, a volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were paused several times before the blast following public outcry and legal challenges.

On Wednesday evening, the Army said that an "all clear" has been issued around the ammunition plant.

President Donald Trump said shortly after the blast that reports showed mitigation efforts "far exceeded expectations".

"The Army's controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success," Adam Telle, acting secretary of the US Army, wrote on social media.

Despite widespread concern from residents of Middletown, Iowa, ahead of the blast, officials have said that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.

In a Wednesday evening update on X, the Army said that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema) had issued the "all clear" around the plant and that there was no airborne lead detection following the detonation.

local.title: Genesee partners with Foodlink for Keg Tree food drive
local.summary: The first 200 people who attend the annual Keg Tree lighting with three nonperishable food items will receive a free commemorative mug.
local.body:
The Genesee Brewery is partnering with Foodlink for the first time to turn its annual Keg Tree lighting into a food drive.

The first 200 people who arrive to the event on Dec. 4 with three non-perishable food items will receive a free mug, shaped like a keg and etched with a picture of the Keg Tree. The food drive will continue through the holiday season at the Genesee Brew House.

Mark Dwyer at Foodlink said the event comes at a pivotal time for food insecurity in Rochester.

"It's a great chance to just raise awareness locally for not only Foodlink and the work that we do, but just the issue of food insecurity that impacts thousands of our neighbors," Dwyer said.

Foodlink tracks data from all of the food pantries in its network around the region. Dwyer said that the numbers of people visiting food pantries from August and September were the highest the nonprofit has ever seen. Those months also saw a 13% increase in food pantry usage compared to the previous year.

"What's on everyone's mind: food, fuel, prices are sky high," Dwyer said. "Just inflation and the economy are continuing to impact people's ability to put food on the table."

The Genesee Brewery approached Foodlink to partner at Keg Tree. Carl Falk, general manager for the Genesee Brew House, said the plan is to focus the company on giving back to the Rochester community.

"Foodlink has been such a staple in our community, helping people, and obviously this time of year there's an even greater emphasis on being a community partner," Falk said.

local.summary: Another round of proposals to close some Buffalo Public Schools is back on the table — one submitted by the interim schools superintendent and another put forward by some board members.
local.body: Another round of proposals to close some Buffalo Public Schools is back on the table — one submitted by the interim schools superintendent and another put forward by some board members.Interim Schools Superintendent Dr. Ebony Prophet-Bullock submitted the district's plan, tweaked from the original that was voted down. It proposes to close the Early Childhood Center, the Bilingual School, Drew Science, Riverside Academy, PS 131 Academy School and East Community High School. However, it no longer includes changes for Middle Early College.“The superintendent's first plan was not a bad plan, just over time, it got really, really muddy up,” stated Erik Bohen, Park District School Board Member.“We have to make sure we do this right and do it well.”But four board members submitted their own proposal. It calls to keep the Early Childhood Center, the Bilingual School and Drew Science open, and instead calls to close the Marva J. Daniel Futures School in the city's Fruit Belt.“The issue is though -- we are running out of money, and we will not have money next year,” declared Bohen.Bohen told me the board could vote Monday night during a special session."I believe 95-percent certain that that will get done," Bohen remarked. “What makes you so confident that it could be done on Monday?” Buckley asked. “Just from my talking's with other board colleagues, I believe no one’s telling me how they're voting but, I believe everybody has their mind made up of where we go, and I believe they've also had pressure from the community as well to get this done," replied Bohen.Both plans still call to phase out Riverside High School.Riverside social studies teacher Marc Bruno told me he doesn't trust the process."This process has been a train wreck from the day it started," Bruno commented. "The trauma that this is putting our students and staff under is unbelievable.”Bruno is questioning the timing of Monday's special meeting."The fact that they announce that there's a special meeting right after we leave for Thanksgiving break on the Monday we get back from break. local.title: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business Saturday
local.summary: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.
local.body: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.Small Business Saturday is this weekend, serving as a community-driven counterpoint to the retail push of Black Friday.I spoke with several Elmwood Village business owners. Tracey Wei, who owns zero-waste home and body care store Little Salmon, described the area as "welcoming and walkable."Wei told me independent businesses like hers often rely on Small Business Saturday to stay afloat."This weekend is like make-or-break for the last quarter," Wei said.Like many businesses in the neighborhood, she'll be holding a sale on Saturday to promote more foot traffic."Businesses need your money more than billionaires, so every dollar you spend, like 70-80% of it stays with the community," she said.WATCH: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business SaturdayOther owners pointed to the unique experience shoppers find in the neighborhood."There are many unique shops you're not gonna find somewhere else, and you get better customer service," Wendie Reed said.At Reed's consignment store, Scoop Shop, shoppers might even find an outfit for the World's Largest Disco on Saturday at the Buffalo Convention Center.Small Business Saturday is one of many events being held to bring people to the area. Seamus Gallivan, the new executive director of the Elmwood Village Association, said the density of the neighborhood is part of its appeal."The beautiful thing about this neighborhood is there are so many businesses so close together that however you get here, you can stay on foot for hours and find everything you need and more," Gallivan explained. He said the stores will also participate in a Christmas window display competition starting December 5. For now, the focus is on bringing people out this Saturday. The day carries real weight for the neighborhood's businesses, said Christa Penner, who owns ShopCraft. local.title: Concerns raised over conditions at cemetery between Colden and Holland
local.summary: Overturned headstones, fallen tree limbs and overgrown vegetation are raising concerns about a cemetery between Colden and Holland.
local.body: Overturned headstones, fallen tree limbs and overgrown vegetation are raising concerns about a cemetery between Colden and Holland.Jeffrey Smith contacted me after visiting the cemetery and becoming concerned about what he found. He said the grounds have not been properly maintained, leaving some burial sites partially obscured by vegetation and debris.“Everything when it was green this summer, you couldn't even see part of these stones because the growth was bad,” Smith said. “And now the leaves and limbs are all over the place.”Smith also pointed to a large tree limb that had fallen near burial sites, raising concerns about the potential for additional damage to headstones.“The big limb just came down over there this year apparently,” he said. “This was here in the spring when we came up and checked.”Smith said veterans are among those buried at the cemetery and believes their graves deserve better care.“All these veterans have served our country," he said. "We should be taking care of their graves." WATCH: Concerns raised over conditions at cemetery between Colden and Holland7 News contacted the Town of Colden to figure out who is responsible for maintaining the property. Documents show that the cemetery is privately owned.Town officials said Scouts sometimes volunteer to help clean up the grounds.7 News also contacted the property owner for comment about the cemetery's condition but did not receive a response. Smith lives nearly two hours away and said he cannot regularly visit to monitor the property. He hopes someone will take action.“I'd like to see it cleaned up, maintained, lawn mowed and for it to look proper,” Smith said.He hopes the cemetery can be restored to a condition that is respectful to the people buried there and the families who come to visit.

local.body:
WESTFIELD — A Portland resident is facing charges after he allegedly spray-painted and attempted to drill a hole into the Lincoln statue in the village.

At approximately 2:42 p.m. Wednesday, the Westfield Police Department responded to a criminal mischief complaint at Main and Portage streets. A male wearing a flannel shirt, later identified as Nicholas A. Rychick, was spray-painting and attempting to drill a hole into the bronze statue of Abraham Lincoln. A bystander confronted Rychick, 37, who fled in a vehicle.

With assistance from the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and New York State Police, officers located Rychick and his vehicle at a residence in Portland. He was taken into custody without incident and transported to WPD.

The investigation determined that Rychick allegedly attempted to drill a hole into the chest of the memorial to place an arrow into the statue but was unsuccessful. He allegedly proceeded to spray-paint the memorial, damaging it and surrounding holiday decorations.

Rychick was arrested on the above charges, processed and released on appearance tickets directing him to appear before the Town of Westfield Court at a later date.

The Westfield Police Department thanks the concerned citizen who intervened, the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and the New York State Police for their assistance.

The statue, which was erected in 1999, showcases unique, bronze statues of Lincoln and Grace Bedell, the girl who suggested that he grow a beard for his presidential campaign.

Grace Bedell, a young girl from Westfield wrote a letter to Mr. Abraham Lincoln, Presidential Candidate, in 1860, encouraging him to “grow whiskers and her brothers would vote for him and he would look nicer.”

local.body:
One person has been found dead after a fire on Bonita Drive in Fluvanna early Tuesday morning.

Ellicott police responded to the fire when it was reported at 5:02 a.m. Tuesday along with Fluvanna volunteer firefighters. Multiple fire departments responded to the scene, where a camper and garage had become engulfed in flames. The Fluvanna Fire Department was able to extinguish the fire in a timely manner.

The Chautauqua County Fire Investigation Team was subsequently called to the scene to investigate the cause and origin of the fire. During the investigation, unidentified human remains were located at the scene.

The Chautauqua County coroner responded to the scene, and the remains were transported to the Medical Examiner's Office for an autopsy.

At this time, the identity of the deceased has not been determined. The investigation remains ongoing, and no further information is being released at this time.

local.title: Brighton preparing for first phase of its Multiversity Trail project
local.summary: The town is focusing on a stretch of the Lehigh Valley Trail that will be part of the network.
local.body:
The town of Brighton has received a $1.4 million grant from the state to improve a section of the Lehigh Valley Trail between the University of Rochester and Rochester Institute of Technology.

The work is part of the town's Multiversity Trail effort that aims to link the university, RIT, and Monroe Community College campuses using the Lehigh Valley Trail and the Erie Canalway Trail. On the Lehigh Valley Trail leg, the town plans to replace most of the surface, among other things.

"It's an old rail trail, the old Lehigh Valley train line, but you know it really needs upgrading, accessibility, signage, drainage issues," Brighton Supervisor Bill Moehle said. "So we'll be able to address all of those and more with this grant."

Moehle added that the town also wants to install flashing beacons at major road crossings that trail users would be able to activate, similar to the Auburn Trail.

Local News Brighton wants to connect bike trails for students at 3 campuses Jeremy Moule The town has three colleges within and along its borders. It wants students at them to be able to easily bike between campuses. The Lehigh Valley Trail work marks the first phase of the Multiversity Trail project. The town plans to put out a request for proposals around design work early next year.

Moehle said the project will benefit more than the college communities. The Lehigh trail is well used, he said, and an important connector for people living on the west side of town.

"It'll focus on the connection between the U of R and RIT because, you know, we have something there to work with," Moehle said. "There is an existing trail, and this will make it really much more user friendly for all users."

local.title: State announces increased road patrols during holiday weekend
local.summary: Motorists heading out for the holiday are being urged to play it safe. On Wednesday, state Gov. Kathy Hochul announced State Police and local law enforcement agencies statewide will increase patrols to target impaired and reckless driving during the Thanksgiving travel season. Funded by the Governor
local.body:
Motorists heading out for the holiday are being urged to play it safe.

On Wednesday, state Gov. Kathy Hochul announced State Police and local law enforcement agencies statewide will increase patrols to target impaired and reckless driving during the Thanksgiving travel season. Funded by the Governor's Traffic Safety Committee (GTSC), the impaired driving enforcement mobilization will run through Sunday.

"As we gather with friends and family to celebrate Thanksgiving, I want to ensure that everyone gets where they are going safely and not have what should be happy memories marred by a preventable tragedy," Hochul said. "I urge drivers to stay alert, stay sober and move over when you see vehicles stopped on the side of the road. If you're in a vehicle, you should wear seat belts or use proper restraint. I thank our law enforcement for sacrificing their time with loved ones to work on Thanksgiving and throughout the holidays to help keep New York's roadways safe."

In addition to increased traffic volume, the Thanksgiving holiday period is also associated with increased alcohol use. During the 2025 Thanksgiving holiday period, law enforcement officers arrested 2,236 drivers for driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs, 12,496 for speeding and also issued 3,075 tickets to unbelted drivers and passengers.

New York State Police Superintendent Steven G. James said, "Our members work vigilantly year-round to keep our roadways safe and prevent the needless tragedies that result from impaired and reckless driving. As always, we will be doing our part to ensure the holidays are safe for all who live in and travel through our great state. Please think twice before getting behind the wheel of a vehicle if you've been drinking. If you have had alcohol, there are several options available that will provide you with a safe ride to your destination. Together, let's make safety a top priority on our roadways this holiday season."

The State Police will supplement regular patrols statewide through efforts including fixed sobriety checkpoints and utilizing Concealed Identity Traffic Enforcement (CITE) patrol vehicles to better spot distracted drivers and those talking or texting on handheld devices. These unmarked vehicles blend in with everyday traffic but are unmistakable as emergency vehicles once the emergency lighting is activated.

Mtorists must follow the state's Move Over law, which was expanded in March 2024 to require drivers to slow down and move over for all vehicles stopped along the roadway if they can safely do so. The Thruway Authority and state Department of Transportation urge motorists to stay alert while driving, slow down and safely move over when they see a vehicle on the side of the road. The lives of motorists, employees, roadway workers and emergency personnel depend on it.

entertainment.summary: The 'Spanish Apartment' and 'Call my Agent!' director will be honored at the 52nd César Awards on Feb. 25.
entertainment.body:
Cédric Klapisch will receive an honorary César Award at the 52nd César Awards, France ‘s equivalent of the Oscars.

The 64-year-old director is best known in France for his L’Auberge Espagnole ( The Spanish Apartment ) trilogy, which followed a group of European students sharing a Barcelona flat. The original 2002 feature was a low-budget breakout which grossed close to $30 million in France and made stars of Romain Duris and Cécile de France. Klapisch shot two sequels: Russian Dolls (2005) and Chinese Puzzle (2013) and a spin-off series Greek Salad (2023) for Amazon Prime Video in France, focusing on the children of the original students. He directed two episode of French breakout series Call My Agent! , a comedic look inside the French entertainment industry, and served as as artistic director for the show’s first season.

Klapisch recently wrapped his 16th feature, the ensemble comedy S’aimer sur Mars starring Charlotte Le Bon, Pio Marmaï, Vincent Macaigne, and Cécile de France, which Studiocanal is co-producing and distributing.

Klapisch will be honored by the French film academy and Canal+ , the co-producer and exclusive broadcaster of the César, at the 2027 ceremony at the Olympia theater in Paris on Feb. 25. The ceremony will air live and unencrypted on Canal+.

entertainment.summary: The brothers reminisced about their "toxic" and "dangerous" teenage rivalry.
entertainment.body:
Charlie Sheen and Emilio Estevez may have eventually shared the screen in films like “Young Guns” and “Men at Work,” but growing up, their off-camera dynamic was rocky at times.

During a recent appearance on Sheen’s “Mostly Sheenius” podcast, the brothers reminisced about their “toxic” and “dangerous” teenage rivalry .

“We didn’t always get along. And we fought a lot as siblings do,” Estevez said, admitting that even filming Super 8 movies together in their youth turned into an “insane” battle over creative control.

Sheen has previously opened up about the complicated dynamic between the two, including feeling excluded during Estevez’s rise in the 1980s “Brat Pack” era .

Long before they were competing for Hollywood roles, however, they were clashing at home — including one explosive high school fight that ended with Sheen swinging a baseball bat and sheriff’s deputies arriving at their front door.

Sheen recalled gearing up for his first high school date at 16 and didn’t want to show up in his “piece of s— Ford Escort,” so he turned to his brother, who turned him down.

“I said, ‘OK, but like, you don’t mean “no” no, because this really matters to me, this is important, man. This girl’s really pretty, I think she likes me, and if I had your car I think everything would work out,'” Sheen recalled pleading, while Estevez admitted he was “just being a douche” by refusing.

Sheen snapped in what he described as a “blackout” rage and hurled a sandwich toward Estevez. Realizing he was “in trouble,” Sheen bolted down the hallway and locked himself in his bedroom.

entertainment.title: Andy Taylor Was Full of Surprises: Six Deep-Dive Career Moments
entertainment.summary: Following his death at the age of 65, Billboard has highlighted some impressive, but overlooked moments from Andy Taylor’s Hall of Fame career.
entertainment.body:
Andy Taylor , the founding guitarist with Duran Duran , who passed away Monday (Nov. 23) following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, aged 65 , just might be the most underrated musician to emerge from the early 1980s.

Taylor, who would also form The Power Station, enjoyed a solo career and was something of a serial collaborator, stood tall in a golden era for electric guitarists. Even the slickest commercial pop songs had destructive guitar solos, the type of which seem to be lost to this generation and last.

Forget the Cold War, there was another arms race where the weapons of choice were plugged-in six-strings, with rows of effects pedals. Eddie Van Halen, Steve Vai, Joe Satriani, The Edge, Steve Stevens, Yngwie Malmsteen, Steve Lukather. It was an expansive group, and Andy Taylor was a member.

Born in Tynemouth and raised in Cullercoats, Northumberland, in north east England, Taylor was the wild boy in Duran Duran – his autobiography from 2008 even carried that title.

Here was a roguish rockstar with fast hands, itchy feet, who didn’t follow trends, but had many, many followers. But because of his breakthrough with Duran Duran, a band that drew a mystifying flood of hate from critics of the time, Taylor’s talents were largely overlooked.

Duran Duran split into two camps following the release of the 1985 James Bond hit “A View To A Kill.” Andy and John Taylor formed The Power Station, the funk-rock supergroup with Robert Palmer at the front, and Tony Thompson at the back, while Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and Roger Taylor launched Arcadia, a collaborative-stacked project that, in an alternative universe, would’ve been Duran Duran’s fourth studio album.

With The Power Station, Andy Taylor was unleashed. We got shredding, finger tapping, the works. Taylor contributed to the Duran Duran album from 1986, Notorious , then he was out. Fifteen years later, he returned to the band with original drummer Roger Taylor, to reunite the Fab Five. He contributed to the 2004 album Astronaut , and again on the 2023 collection Danse Macabre .

The music world learned of his illness when, in 2022 , Duran Duran was inducted into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame. Taylor, his bandmates explained, as they read out a letter from the guitarist, was unable to attend due to illness.

entertainment.title: ‘South Park’ Season Finale Drops Kenny Into ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ as South America Comes Clean
entertainment.summary: Power outages, penis billionaires and an undead Kenny collide as the season ties up (most of) its loose ends.
entertainment.body:
Logo text All is not well in South America (née South Park ) in the season 29 finale. The long-anticipated November release of Grand Theft Auto VI — the show’s metaphorical stand-in for the midterm elections — has finally arrived, but rolling power outages caused by local billionaires’ AI-powered data centers are keeping the townspeople — from the little-seen Goth Kids to Mr. Garrison to Big Gay Al, and of course, our core boy heroes — from enjoying the biggest media release of all time.

Mass protest ensues, and we’re reminded of the deep corruption that has taken hold of the Colorado town, starting with Mayor McDaniels’ administration taking kickbacks from the tiny-penis billionaires — who, we’ll recall, broke Butters’ fight against them earlier in the season with a backroom deal to keep building their data centers in town and siphoning its power. Butters and family deliver a fun nod to “It’s a Good Life,” a classic Twilight Zone plot here, with Butters’ parents believing he has supernatural powers and are absolutely terrified of him. Related Stories TV 'South Park' Takes Aim at Jensen Huang, Nvidia Spy Scandal in Next Episode Business Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

For an episode that packs plenty in, calling back to much of the season’s action and picking up most of the plot threads it introduced (minus, unfortunately, the great Tweek and Craig ), it’s Lu Kim, the Asian American owner of City Wok and now City Ending massage, who walks away with the heaviest storyline. He’s quickly scapegoated and placed under suspicious watch by armed South America residents, who are made aware of a Chinese spy that feels a little like a recent international tech world scandal. A Shitty Ending feels inevitable.

Meanwhile, Kenny, who was believed to have died in an e-bike accident in the season premiere, resurfaces terrifyingly. The boys first spot him in the distance outside; after following him, they discover he’s a zombie. He points at them horrifically, à la Donald Sutherland in Invasion of the Body Snatchers , then disintegrates before their eyes. He later reemerges to haunt them in the worst place imaginable: inside Grand Theft Auto VI as the boys play. Their supposedly deceased friend exits the game as some sort of four-legged beast, ready to devour little Butters.

Whatever is going on here, our longtime elementary school heroes are going to figure it out — and in doing so, tie up all (well, most) of the season’s threads. Shaken to his core by Kenny’s appearance, Butters fesses up about the billionaires’ earlier bribe, then tells the boys how he offloaded the data centers to Peter Mullins’ house. The boys head there next and discover a high-tech data center in their classmate’s never-looked-at backyard.

entertainment.title: Former Disney Boss Bob Iger Got Employee Pregnant During Extramarital Affair, New Book Claims
entertainment.summary: In 'The House of Mouse,' author Robbie Whelan also claims Iger was frustrated with his compensation.
entertainment.body:
Bob Iger ‘s compensation frustrations and an extramarital affair with an ABC employee that resulted in a pregnancy are some of the revelations laid out in an upcoming tell-all book.

The House of Mouse , written by longtime Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan, is an unauthorized biography and corporate history of the former Disney CEO that releases Dec. 1. Iger reportedly declined to be interviewed for the book.

In the book, Whelan claimed Iger had an extramarital affair with an ABC marketer in the early 1990s while he was running ABC Entertainment at the time, according to The New York Times , which obtained an advance copy. The relationship was consensual. (Iger was previously married to Susan Iger from 1977 to 1994 and married his current wife, Willow Bay, in 1995.) Five Films Later, He's the Keeper of Panem Beyond the Book 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians': How Season 3 Brings Epic Moments to Life and Deals With Annabeth's Absence in the Books

The woman, who wasn’t identified, became pregnant and “suffered through a traumatic termination procedure,” Mr. Whelan wrote. The Times noted that Whelan contrasts Iger’s personal relationship with his public support for the #MeToo movement in the late 2010s.

Elsewhere in the book, it also claimed the former Disney boss was irritated and vindictive when it came to money. In 2025, Iger received a total compensation package of $45.8 million from the company, an increase from his $41.1 million in 2024, The Hollywood Reporter previously reported.

“I am frustrated about compensation! I had a nasty and distasteful negotiation to extend my contract this last time,” Iger allegedly wrote in a private email in 2014 that was sent to Ike Perlmutter, then Marvel’s chairman and a major Disney shareholder, that Whelan obtained. In 2014, Iger earned $46.5 million, a 36 percent increase from the year prior.

Iger served as Disney CEO twice, first from 2005 to 2020 before he returned in 2022 when Bob Chapek was ousted . Josh D’Amaro took over in March of this year after Iger stepped down.

In The House of Mouse , Iger wasn’t the only Disney exec facing scathing accusations during their time running the company. Whelan also accused Chapek of mocking fans at a Marvel movie premiere in 2022.

entertainment.summary: The Rock Hall-inducted group headlined the halftime show, which streamed live late Wednesday, Nov. 25 on Netflix.
entertainment.body:
The legendary Irish rock band, as they’ve done so often in the past, stepped into the cauldron, rocked out, and gave everyone what they were looking for.

On this occasion, Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. stepped into the colosseum that is the NFL ‘s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium, pitting the Los Angeles Rams against the visiting Green Bay Packers. Explore Bono U2 See latest videos, charts and news

The Rock Hall-inducted group headlined the halftime show, which streamed live late Wednesday, Nov. 25 on Netflix. At the very top, the four bandmates took the long walk to the centerfield as a choir recited the lyrics of “I Still Haven’t Found What I’m Looking For.”

“Thank you for having us,” Bono remarked over Mullen’s iconic, military-style drum pattern that launched the mini-set proper with “Sunday Bloody Sunday,” one of the band’s early political anthems. The production stepped up several gears as a marching band assembled and the song shapeshifted, interpolating The Supremes’ “Stop! In The Name of Love.”

Then, a change in mood as U2 paid tribute to Dolly Parton , the late queen of country’s smiling image splashed on three sails towering over the circular, center stage. Bono dueted with Dolly’s vocals for “Torn,” her very last recording which appears on the band’s 16th and latest studio album, Carnaval de Luz .

And, in a moment that earned a roar from the audience, the band slotted seamlessly into another Joshua Tree number, “Where The Streets Have No Name.” The sails came down, and U2 got down to rockstar business — with some support from scores of backing singers.

Without missing a beat, Bono and Co. reached into their glorybox with a rendition of “Pride (In The Name of Love)” a tribute to the assassinated civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., which appeared on their 1984 LP The Unforgettable Fire. And with that, U2 was done and it was game on.

entertainment.summary: Bella Hadid is sharing new revelations about her health. The 30-year-old explained how managing several medical conditions in addition to Lyme disease—which her mom, Yolanda Hadid, first shared...
entertainment.body:
The 30-year-old explained how managing several medical conditions in addition to Lyme disease—which her mom, Yolanda Hadid , first shared her daughter had in 2015 —impacts her, explaining, "My body just can’t connect with my brain."

"I have POTS, and I have a lot of PMDD, endometriosis," Bella told Harper's Bazaar in an interview published Nov. 23. "Plus my Lyme and things that affect my body very deeply."

While premenstrual dysphoric disorder and endometriosis are illnesses related to the female reproductive system that cause painful and exhausting menstrual cycles, according to the Cleveland Clinic, postural orthostatic tachycardia is a syndrome that causes a person's heart to beat faster when they change the position of their body.

And in speaking about her diagnoses, the Beauty actress was brought back to a time when a frightening flare-up threatened to keep her off the runway.

"Right before I walked out on the runway for my opening look, I went to go stretch and my whole clavicle completely—," she recounted. "I don’t even know what it was. My lungs almost collapsed, and I couldn’t breathe."

And with her following the family business in fashion along with Yolanda's other two kids, Gigi Hadid , 31, and Anwar Hadid , 27, Bella admitted the painful interruptions shake her confidence to perform.

"My body goes through these different motions of feeling really good and then all of a sudden crashing on me at the worst moments," she continued. "Because I know how to walk. One thing I can do is I can strut. But it’s a lot of pressure; we all have our own insecurities."

With that in mind, the Victoria's Secret Angel has to remind herself, "maybe my body can’t handle all that I have going on," which ultimately results in the freedom to decide, "'No, we can’t do that today.'"

entertainment.body:

entertainment.title: Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys
entertainment.summary: The late guitarist gave the band an aggressive edge that no other New Romantic act had — which is part of the reason the songs never fade into the past
entertainment.body:
Farewell to Andy Taylor , the bad boy in Duran Duran , the loose cannon, the purest rocker in the band. He was the guitarist who brought his own style of glam-rock flash to their classic Eighties hits, from “Hungry Like the Wolf” to “Girls on Film” to “Rio.” He gave them an aggressive edge that no other New Romantic band had — part of the reason these songs never fade into the past. The band announced his death today, at 65, after a long fight with prostate cancer.

The tragic news comes at a tough time for Duran Duran fans, just days after original drummer Roger Taylor announced he was stepping down because of his tinnitus. That leaves bassman John Taylor as the last of the band’s three Taylors. (None of whom were related.)

“He brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music,” Duran Duran said in a statement. “His playing drove the songs that took us around the world and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge.”

Andy Taylor was the original guitarist from their early days, but he quit in 1986, at the peak of their fame. “It’s like one of those rat wheels, isn’t it?” he said in the 2018 documentary Duran Duran: There’s Something You Should Know . “And you just gotta be King Rat sometimes and say, ‘Bollocks! I’m jumping off!’”

He grew up in a fishing town near Newcastle and played his earliest gigs at military bases around Europe. But he took the train down to Birmingham when he saw a “guitarist wanted” ad in the British music paper Melody Maker. In the band’s first Rolling Stone cover story, in 1984 , he told the story of his audition for Duran Duran. “They were quite blatant,” Andy said. “They said, ‘We’re poseurs. We want a good-looking poseur band.’” But for Andy, that was no problem. “I said, ‘Good, because I like dressing up and I love wearing makeup.’”

These were fighting words, calculated to shock and outrage any old-school rock traditionalists who might be reading. And it worked — Duran Duran were a massively divisive band, especially in America. But it sums up the brazen attitude he brought to the band. Brash, Andy was. entertainment.title: Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor looked happy while greeting fans in last public sighting before his death

entertainment.body:
Andy Taylor was all smiles while greeting fans in London during his last public sighting before his death at the age of 65.

The late Duran Duran guitarist appeared in good spirits signing autographs and soaking up the love from his admirers as he left Wogan House after appearing on Zoe Ball’s since-ended BBC Radio 2 show on Aug. 30, 2023.

Taylor wore a Calvin Klein bucket hat, dark sunglasses, a black AllSaints jacket, a tiger-printed button-up shirt and Adidas sneakers for the outing.

The musician died on Monday after a “long and courageous battle” with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer , his band and family announced via a joint statement Wednesday.

According to the statement, he “passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family.”

“To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather,” Taylor’s wife, Tracey, wrote. “He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first.”

“Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home,” she continued.

Tracey praised Andy for battling cancer over the “last few years with so much courage and determination.”

entertainment.title: Blade Runner 2099 Has A Major Problem That Goes Back To The Original 1982 Movie
entertainment.summary: Prime Video's new miniseries starring Hunter Schafer, Blade Runner 2099, is a follow-up to the movies Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049, but it has a problem.
entertainment.body:
Clay Enos/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Ironically, Prime's "Blade Runner 2099" is a program about the future, and it's stuck in the early 1980s. Showrunner Silka Luisa's limited series beams reverence for the classic proto-cyberpunk film that launched the franchise, and that fidelity to the urtext can be a benefit ... it can also be a hazard.

In "2099," bioengineered replicants have conquered organic mankind; elite LAPD officers known as blade runners hunt down uncooperative humans. Throughout the first four episodes, blade runners Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) and "Marian" — an undercover human whose real name is Cora (Hunter Schafer) — search for Marek (Johnny Harris), who's Olwen's ex and a person of interest to the underground resistance network that Cora works for. In Episode 4, Olwen finally learns why Marek went AWOL: He's searching for a golden orb believed to contain a memory from the long-deceased inventor of replicants, Eldon Tyrell, that holds the secret to open-ended replicant longevity.

Olwen has only eight days left to live, so Marek's quest to save her is very admirable. It is also very familiar. In director Ridley Scott's original "Blade Runner" from 1982 — a movie very loosely based on "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" by Philip K. Dick – a gang of replicants led by Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer) sneaks into Los Angeles to corner and confront their creator, tech oligarch Eldon Tyrell (Joe Turkel), to demand an expansion to their four-year lifespan.

Warner Bros./YouTube Not only does another story about replicants who quite understandably want to live longer feel very redundant, but it also relitigates a problem the "Blade Runner" version of civilization solved more than 50 years ago in its canonical past. In 1982's "Blade Runner," we learn the Tyrell Corporation created replicants primarily for treacherous grunt work in space. To prevent them from rising up and overthrowing their oppressors, Tyrell engineered replicants to live for a limited time — four years in the case of Nexus-6 models — and then automatically die, hence Roy's righteous fury.

Director Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" emerged as a long overdue sequel in 2017. None of the numerous replicants in "2049" appear concerned about a hard deadline. When K (Ryan Gosling) finds him early in the film, Nexus-8 model Sapper Morton (Dave Bautista) says he's been living and working on his protein farm since 2020 – which makes him considerably older than 4. In a short "2049" prequel film set in 2036, Niander Wallace (Jared Leto) — a mad scientist and business demon whose Wallace Corporation supplants the bankrupt Tyrell Corporation — claims the replicants he designs can live as long or as briefly as he designs them to. He probably isn't exaggerating.
