entertainment.title: FCC Bid Challenging ABC’s TV Licenses Halted in Major Win for Network
entertainment.summary: The ruling is a major setback for the administration in the government's campaign against ABC and national media.
entertainment.body:
Logo text ABC has won a court order barring the Federal Communications Commission from taking further action against the network amid the government’s efforts to possibly strip the company of its local broadcast licenses.

U.S. District Judge Loren Alikhan on Wednesday rebuffed the FCC ‘s bid to dismiss the lawsuit, finding that the agency likely violated ABC’s First Amendment rights by weaponizing its regulatory authority to retaliate against the network for protected speech and pressure it to change its editorial decisions.

“Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration,” an ABC News spokesperson said in a statement. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: 'Dancing With the Stars' Records Another Huge Finale TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Names Historic Season 35 Winner: See All the Scores, Who Won

The Disney-owned company sued the FCC earlier this year after the Brendan Carr-led agency called for an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses. The renewal prompted concerns of retaliation since it followed an investigation into Disney’s diversity practices and ABC late-night host Kimmy Kimmel angering President Donald Trump with a joke.

In Wednesday’s ruling, the court said that Carr’s conduct is “powerful evidence” of the FCC’s “retaliatory motive.”

“It is no coincidence that President Trump criticized Mr. Kimmel’s skit on social media and the very next day Defendants initiated the early license renewal proceedings,” Alikhan wrote. She pointed to Carr’s comment that “we can do this the easy way or the hard way” and that “these companies can find ways to take action on Kimmel, or there is going to be additional work for the FCC ahead.”

The FCC has maintained that the early license renewal proceedings are merely “in aid” of its investigation into Disney’s employment practices and would’ve occurred regardless.

The court was unconvinced, finding that it “does not find that explanation to be credible.” It stressed that Trump has targeted ABC for several years.

entertainment.title: How The One Ring Helps Sauron Control The Other Rings Of Power
entertainment.summary: "The Rings of Power" season 3 finale shows but a glimpse of the One Ring's immense power, leaving us with a lot to look forward to in season 4.
entertainment.body:
New Line Cinema Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 – "The Doom of Men"

"The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 sees Sauron finally wielding his One Ring of power — that is, until he takes it off and surrenders to his enemies. Don't worry, there's more to that move than the Dark Lord willingly giving up. He'll be back. When Sauron first forges the One Ring at the end of Episode 7 , he puts it on, and the Elven ring-bearers immediately remove their own overpowered jewelry. They're aware of the Dark Lord, and they don't want to be controlled by him. But what exactly does the One Ring do to allow the Dark Lord to control the other Rings of Power?

Tolkien doesn't give a clear, scientific answer here. But in "The Silmarillion" he does provide a good summary: "Now the Elves made many rings; but secretly Sauron made One Ring to rule all the others, and their power was bound up with it, to be subject wholly to it and to last only so long as it too should last." The book explains that Sauron pours much of his own strength and will into his Ring so it can control the others, saying, "while he wore the One Ring, he could perceive all the things that were done by means of the lesser rings, and he could see and govern the very thoughts of those that wore them."

Prime Video The One Ring rules the others. There's no doubt about that. In a letter to a publisher in 1951, Tolkien clarified the power of the One Ring over other rings, adding to the description that, along with containing all of the powers of the other Rings, it could see the thoughts and govern their behavior "and in the end could utterly enslave them."

However, the way the One Ring controls the wearers of the "lesser rings" of power isn't consistent. A lot of this depends on who's wearing them. The Elves, for instance, are instantly aware of Sauron when he puts on the One Ring. They're able to understand what's happening and have the willpower to take off their Rings and hide them.

In contrast, the Nine Rings for Mortal Men give Sauron complete control over their owners. "The Silmarillion" says, "They fell under the thraldom of the ring that they bore and under the domination of the One, which was Sauron's." Even when Sauron doesn't have the One Ring, he still has a degree of slavish control over these Men. (What's Elrond's line again? Men are weak.)

She then raised the stakes considerably, claiming Pitt had turned “physically and emotionally abusive” toward her and their children during an outburst on a private plane in 2016 that led to the collapse of their marriage. Jolie said she initially considered selling her stake in Miraval to Pitt, realizing it would eventually go to their children, but the deal fell apart when Pitt allegedly demanded a non-disparagement clause she blasted as an “unconscionable gag order.”

On Wednesday, the former Hollywood power couple announced they reached a private settlement in their nearly five-year legal war, heading off a public and potentially bruising trial set for next August.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” Pitt and Jolie said in a joint statement issued by their representatives. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”

As of Wednesday afternoon, no request for dismissal appeared on the court docket. A review of the previously contentious case remained scheduled for Dec. 7.

sports.title: Jayden Daniels: Brandon Aiyuk and I put the past behind us
sports.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media.
sports.body:
“I’m a grown man, he’s a grown man,” Daniels said. “Things happen. You don’t know what he was going through. You don’t know what I was going through at that time.”

Daniels said he looked up to Aiyuk when they were at Arizona State together and thinks they can have a good relationship as teammates again.

“That’s somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU,” Daniels said. “So, like I said, I know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle our differences and just move forward from there. That’s like a brother to me. Like I said, we’ve been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, just put the past behind us.”

As for the social media posts that Aiyuk made, Daniels said he was never angry about that.

“I prayed for him because he’s like family to me,” Daniels said. “I think that was a very dark moment in his life.”

Daniels declined to go into specifics about recent conversations with Aiyuk but said he hopes Aiyuk will be a good addition to the Commanders.

“That’s between us, personal, but yeah, we did chat,” Daniels said. “He works hard. Before his knee injury he was All-Pro, very explosive, big catch radius, so excited for him to have a fresh start, new opportunity to prove himself day in and day out.”

Aiyuk hasn’t played in more than two years, but he was once one of the best receivers in the NFL. If Aiyuk can play at anything close to the level he used to play at, he can be a significant addition to the Commanders’ offense. Daniels is excited about that possibility.

sports.title: T.J. Lang blasts "despicable" Aaron Rodgers comments about Mike McCarthy
sports.summary: T.J.
sports.body:
Lang sharply criticized Rodgers for his decision to go public with issues that should have stayed in the Pittsburgh locker room.

“ I think it’s despicable ,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit, via Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing . “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media.

“He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just — he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. It’s a victim mentality. It’s a ‘poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that.’ And I’m sick, man.

“I’ve been in a group chat with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.”

Most football players would feel that way. There’s a code in the locker room. Rodgers violated it.

“Mike McCarthy was my head coach for 8 years, and I love Mike McCarthy,” Lang said. “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and still have a great relationship with him.

“I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably 5 years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike.”

Rodgers isn’t a whistleblower. He’s a troublemaker. He didn’t get his way, so he emptied a can of gasoline and tossed a match over his shoulder on the way out the door.

sports.title: Rams shut down Packers in second half for a 26-13 win in NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game
sports.summary: The Rams running game powered them to their fifth straight win.
sports.body:
Blake Corum ran for 151 yards and a score in final 30 minutes and the Rams defense shut out the Packers to pave the way to a 26-13 win. The victory is the fifth in a row for the Rams and they are now 7-4 with a Thursday night home game against the Chiefs on deck in Week 13.

The win moves the Rams ahead of the Packers in the race for NFC playoff spots and Thursday’s game between the Lions and Bears will have further impact on the chances for all four teams to advance to the postseason.

Corum’s touchdown came at the end of the Rams’ first possession of the second half and he finished the game with a career-high 32 carries for 184 yards.

That scoring drive ate up more than eight minutes. The Packers had a quick three-and-out, but briefly showed some life when linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper picked off Matthew Stafford to set the offense up in Los Angeles territory. Jordan Love turned the ball right back over when he hung a deep pass that safety Jaylen McCullough snagged out of the air. The Rams would then ride Corum and Kyren Williams on a pair of drives that covered more than 11 minutes.

The Packers’ last chance came with 6:13 left and they moved the ball to midfield before Love threw his second interception of the game. Cornerback Emmanuel Forbes got that one and the Packers were out of timeouts well before the two-minute warning.

Sticking with the ground game helped to limit Packers defensive end Micah Parsons’s impact in his return from last season’s torn ACL. He had a sack late in the first half, but Stafford only threw eight times after the break and the Packers’ run defense could not get their offense the ball often enough to get back into the game.

Love was 17-of-29 for 198 yards and a touchdown, but clearly missed wide receiver Christian Watson after he left the game with a concussion. They only picked up two first downs after halftime and they’ll hope that an extended break before their Week 13 trip to New Orleans is enough time for him to return to action.

The Rams have several injuries of their own to monitor as guard Bill Murray joined tight ends Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee in making early exits from the game. They’d like to have all those players back next week, but they showed on Wednesday night that Corum can sometimes be enough all by himself.

sports.title: On Our Way Home is free on Thursday and Friday

The On Our Way Home ebook is available for free on Thursday and Friday.

Why not give something away? This is the week when everyone is trying to sell you something. No one is giving you anything, with zero strings attached.

On Our Way Home is primarily a Christmas story. It’s also a ghost story. I cranked it out between Thanksgiving and New Year’s Day a few years back.

In the interests of avoiding any spoilers, I’ll just say this: Download it and give it a try. It’s essentially about family and redemption and reconciliation. It’s also about forgiving others, while finding a way to forgive yourself.

It’s funny at times. It’s sad at times. If you make it to the end, you’ll possibly shed a tear or two.

The best feedback I’ve gotten came from a reader who had suffered from PTSD for years. Reading On Our Way Home unlocked his ability to feel emotions again.

I never intended anything like that. I just had an idea for a story, years before writing it. One year, I got caught up in the spirit of the season and it flowed, one chapter, one page, one word at a time.

The price is right. If you don’t like it, delete it. If you like it, keep going.

sports.title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
sports.summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
sports.body:
We’ve reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team’s other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, “ Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback .”

On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet.

Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II but from team spokesman Burt Lauten — that Mason Rudolph will start on Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive.

The news forced the Broncos to make a quick pivot in their preparations from Rodgers to Rudolph. As one source put it, the Broncos weren’t sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing .

It was definitely a bad thing, all things considered, for the Steelers.

By Wednesday morning, reports emerged that it was a coach’s decision . At 8:00 a.m. ET, McCarthy informed the team of the decision.

Enter Pat McAfee. He teased a surprise guest at 1:40 p.m. ET. As expected, it was Rodgers.

sports.title: Micah Parsons gets first sack of season, Packers and Rams tied 13-13 at halftime
sports.summary: Parsons's sack came just before end of the first half in Los Angeles.
sports.body:
Parsons made his return from a torn ACL against the Rams and had a couple of pressures early in the game. He got home for a sack of Matthew Stafford on the Rams’ first play after a Trey Smack field goal tied the score at 13-13 with 1:50 to play in the half.

The Rams ran out the clock from there and they will get the ball to start the second half at SoFi Stadium.

Parsons’s sack was part of an eventful final couple of minutes. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and Watson is now being evaluated for a concussion. It would be a big loss for the Packers as Watson has four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown so far on Wednesday night.

Running back Kyren Williams scored the Rams’ only touchdown, but their offense slowed down after picking up points on each of their first three possessions. Stafford is 12-of-15 for 98 yards while Williams and Blake Corum have 35 yards on nine carries.

Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 12-of-18 for 154 yards. The Packers will be hoping for right guard Kevin Zeitler’s return from an ankle injury while waiting for more word on Watson and the Rams called tight end Davis Allen to return from an ankle injury.

sports.title: Rams S Kamren Kinchens ejected for hit on Christian Watson
sports.summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson.
sports.body:
Per the Netflix broadcast, the league office said that Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and making helmet-to-helmet contact with Watson and NFL executive vice president Troy Vincent made the final call on disqualifying him from the game.

Watson held onto the ball, but went to the locker room with members of the medical staff and the catch did not count because Packers wideout Matthew Golden was flagged for offensive pass interference to offset the Kinchens foul.

The play came on a fourth-and-1 and the Packers ultimately opted to kick a field goal rather than go for it again. It is now 13-13 with under two minutes to play in the half.

sports.title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson cut Rams lead to 13-10
sports.summary: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium.
sports.body:
A little more than three minutes after the Rams scored their first touchdown of the night, the Packers paid their first visit to the end zone. Jordan Love hooked up with Christian Watson for a six-yard score that cut the Rams’ lead to 13-10 with just over eight minutes to play in the half.

Watson also caught a pass on the first play of the drive and that completion went for 21 yards. Love hit Watson’s fellow wideout Matthew Golden for a 39-yard gain on the next play and the quarterback scrambled for the third first down of the possession a couple of plays after that big gain.

The Packers went three-and-out and turned the ball over on their first two possessions, but they are now outgaining the Rams thanks to back-to-back scoring drives.

sports.title: Kyren Williams makes it 13-3 Rams in second quarter
sports.summary: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points.
sports.body:
Running back Kyren Williams finished off the third possession with a seven-yard sprint into the end zone that pushed the Rams’ lead over the Packers to 13-3 with 11:29 to play in the first half. It’s the first time the Rams have scored on their first three possessions this season and it’s also the first time the Packers have allowed their opponents points on their first three drives.

Most of the other movement on the drive came through the air. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed passes to Williams, tight end Davis Allen, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, and tight end Tyler Higbee for first downs before Williams’s touchdown. The throw to Williams came just before Stafford took a hit from Packers defensive end Micah Parsons.

Stafford is 10-of-12 for 87 yards while Jordan Love is 6-of-10 for 70 yards, including a 32-yarder to Christian Watson that set up Trey Smack’s 54-yard field goal.

The Rams picked up a first down when Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt was flagged for roughing Matthew Stafford and added another on a 15-yard pass to Konata Mumpfield. Packers defensive end Micah Parsons pressured Stafford into an incompletion on the next play and a botched backward pass cost the Rams six yards before they settled for Brandon McManus’s second field goal.

sports.body: Well, the NFL went and found reason to schedule a game on a Wednesday, crowning what’s certain to become it’s own brand of holiday with what’s been dubbed “The Thanksgiving Eve” game. In the early decades of the NFL preceding the 1940s — back when lights on funny looking cars, street lamps, and those indoors were still sometimes powered by oil and kerosene, and a short while later by carbide gas — Wednesday games were not unusual. Since 1940? Before tonight, six NFL games of notoriety were played on a Wednesday in the last 86 years, and none from 1949 through 2011. Do you know when the most recent game was played before this evening’s matchup? * September 22, 1948: Los Angeles Rams vs. Detroit Lions (First Wednesday game after 1940) * September 5, 2012: Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants (Moved from Thursday to avoid President Obama’s DNC speech) * December 2, 2020: Baltimore Ravens vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (COVID-19-rescheduled game) * December 25, 2024: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Steelers (Christmas Day game) * December 25, 2024: Ravens vs. Houston Texans (Christmas Day game) * September 9, 2026: Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots (2026 NFL season opener ahead of Thursday game in Australia) Yesterday’s NFL is not today’s NFL, and with each of today’s games put in front of scores of holiday eyes, new interest grows. The move lately has been to put juicy matchups in the best slots of each major holiday. But tonight? This evening, the Los Angeles Rams, Green Bay Packers, and the NFL get a new “holiday” all to themselves. Okay, maybe they’ll have to fight for the attention of people out at informal high school reunions, but you know the game’s going to be on even at Applebee’s. (The impetus for that behemoth’s name is as thrilling as you might guess.) But here we are as a species, soaking in every single second of NFL football available to us. Truth be told, tonight’s game has real potential to be great. Two 6-4 teams are fighting to remain in playoff contention, with Green Bay hanging on to the seventh (and last) seed in the current NFL playoff race. If the regular season ended today, the Rams would be watching the postseason from home as the ninth seed in the NFC. Rooting interests? It’s another NFC-NFC game, so nothing carries too much weight. sports.title: Steelers should have known Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy couldn't co-exist
sports.summary: Someone in the organization should have said a reunion cannot happen.
sports.body:
The reporting of Tyler Dunne, who at the time wrote for Bleacher Report , made it clear that there were issues between them during the latter years of McCarthy’s time with the Packers. Rodgers took it to another level on Wednesday, telling Pat McAfee and company that McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired by the Packers — and that McCarthy had done some of the things he’s been doing with the Steelers when McCarthy coached the Packers.

If McCarthy believes Rodgers got him fired by the Packers, why in the world would McCarthy want Rodgers in his Pittsburgh locker room? It’s ludicrous. It’s asinine. It’s self-destructive.

From Rodgers’s perspective, why in the world would he want to play for McCarthy again? Although Rodgers said Wednesday that he believed McCarthy would be different given it’s Rodgers’s last year in the NFL and McCarthy’s first year in his dream job, it was naive for Rodgers to think that, at 63, McCarthy would suddenly start working harder than he ever has.

Oh, they tried to sell us on the idea that he would. “ Attention to detail ” became a talking point during training camp. Plenty of media members swallowed the hook.

Rodgers knew better. But he ignored his own experiences with McCarthy — in the same way McCarthy ignored his own experiences with Rodgers.

The situation cried out for someone, anyone in the organization to stand up and say, “Are we nuts? Once adversity strikes, this situation will crumble. And it will take us with it.”

It didn’t just crumble. It imploded into one of the most embarrassing situations any NFL franchise has endured in years, if not ever.

As the saying goes, when you dance with the devil, you don’t change the devil. The devil changes you. By allowing McCarthy and Rodgers to reprise their Lambeau rumba, the Steelers thought the music would stop in the postseason. Instead, McCarthy and Rodgers have pulled a franchise with six Super Bowl trophies into the eighth circle of dysfunction.

sports.title: Report: G.M. Omar Khan called Aaron Rodgers directly to inform him of the benching
sports.summary: As expected, the Steelers view the events that resulted in the benching and eventual release of quarterback Aaron Rodgers differently than Rodgers does.
sports.body:
On one very specific point — as it relates to whether the Steelers properly handled the situation — the Steelers and Rodgers sharply disagree.

Rodgers said Wednesday that he learned he’d be benched and inactive when tight end Pat Freiermuth called Rodgers, after the announcement of the move was made at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday night. However, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported during the Wednesday night pregame show that G.M. Omar Khan called Rodgers to inform him of the change to Mason Rudolph.

It’s odd, to say the least, that the Steelers announced the move after 11:00 p.m. local time on a Tuesday night. If Rodgers didn’t know, there was no reason to let the world (and specifically the Broncos) know the move had been made.

The mere fact that the Steelers announced it when they did suggests that Rodgers knew about the decision, and that the Steelers believed he possibly would release it in terms that supported his broader version of the events.

By announcing it on Tuesday night, the Steelers pre-empted a late-night social-media post from Rodgers — or a strategic leak to a reporter — painting the situation in the light most favorable to Rodgers. For example, Rodgers could have characterized that he was benched because he was repeatedly blowing the whistle internally about coach Mike McCarthy’s various alleged lapses.

While it’s a minor point, it points to the broader issue of credibility. If Rodgers knew about the decision, any suggestion that he didn’t would be calculated to make the Steelers look inept for telling the world he’d been benched without letting him know about it in advance.

The truth may never be fully known. But it’s clear that, as to the things that happened over the past day or two, there are (as there always seems to be) two versions — Rodgers’s version and the team’s version.

It’s also possible there are three versions. Rodgers’s version, the Steelers’ version, and the truth.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy: Aaron Rodgers made an ultimatum outside his job description

sports.body:
“There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him,” McCarthy said.

Asked to explain what he meant by that, McCarthy wouldn’t directly answer.

“I’m not going to get into all those specifics. I know you have to ask the question, but those conversations are better served — they’re private conversations,” McCarthy told reporters.

McCarthy said he and every player should take pride in being a Pittsburgh Steeler, and conduct himself like a Steeler.

“We’re all fortunate to work here. This is an incredible opportunity, to work for the Pittsburgh Steelers,” McCarthy said.

The most direct answer McCarthy gave to a question today was when a reporter asked if Rodgers had been released. McCarthy simply answered, “Yes.”

sports.title: Report: Mike McCarthy "has the full support" of the Steelers organization
sports.summary: The Steelers are planning no "immediate" changes.
sports.body:
Via ESPNFL, McCarthy “ has the full support of the organization ,” and "[t]hey are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes.”

The use of the term “immediate” is curious. Is this just a matter of getting through the season before taking a closer look at the situation?

Regardless, Rodgers dropped a fairly sizable turd into the confluence of the Ohio, Allegheny, and Monongahela Rivers. If his claims about McCarthy are true, McCarthy is objectively unfit to coach the team.

At this point, there’s not much that can be done. They play a game on Friday afternoon. Besides, they’re 6-4 and fighting for a spot in the playoffs.

While the situation is far from ideal, the Steelers are opting to stay the course for now. Likely because it’s too late to change direction.

The real question is whether, after the season, McCarthy will be given a chance to step down. And, if not, whether he’ll be fired.

Barring a postseason berth and the first playoff win since the 2016 season, it’s hard to envision the situation being sustainable. Which could result in a team that had three coaches from 1969 through 2025 having two in two years.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy confirms he said "1-2-3 Packers" at halftime last Sunday

After saying head coach Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meetings and missed other ones altogether in his first comments since being benched on Tuesday night, Rodgers said that McCarthy broke down the team in the locker room with “1-2-3 Packers” in reference to the team he coached through the 2018 season. In a press conference later in the day, McCarthy confirmed that happened but said he took issue with how Rodgers characterized other things that included his commitment to the job.

“The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional. . . . Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments,” McCarthy said.

The Steelers have released Rodgers and McCarthy stressed the need for the team to focus on Friday’s game against the Broncos, although it feels like that’s going to be difficult based on how the last 18 hours have played out in Pittsburgh.

sports.title: Steelers could try to not pay Aaron Rodgers the balance of his $22 million salary
sports.summary: If/when the Steelers release quarterback Aaron Rodgers, they'll have to decide whether to willingly pay the balance of his $22 million base salary, or whether to fight.
sports.body:
With his Week 12 paycheck already vested, the question becomes Week 13 through Week 18. Six weeks, totaling $7.33 million.

It won’t be easy to cut him off. First, the Steelers would have to release him for reasons unrelated to skill, injury, or salary cap. The argument, if the Steelers make it, would be that Rodgers’s appearance on Pat McAfee’s show constitutes personal conduct detrimental to the interests of the team .

A grievance would undoubtedly be filed, if the Steelers pursue that approach.

But even without the guarantee, Rodgers’s presence on the Week 1 roster qualifies him for the balance of his base salary as “termination pay” under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. To circumvent that, the Steelers would have to show that Rodgers has become ineligible for termination pay.

Here’s the key language, from Article 30, Section 3(b) of the CBA: “An otherwise qualified player will not be entitled to Termination Pay if (i) the Club terminated the player’s contract for Conduct Detrimental to the Club, and (ii) the Non-Injury Grievance Arbitrator determines that the player’s conduct was so severe that the maximum discipline for Conduct Detrimental of a fine equal to one week’s salary and suspension without pay for four weeks, pursuant to Article 42, Section 1(b)(xvii) of this Agreement (regardless of whether the Club imposed any such discipline prior to terminating the player’s contract), constitutes an inadequate remedy for the player’s conduct.”

It won’t be easy to satisfy that standard. But there’s language in the CBA that potentially applies to Rodgers’s public comments from Wednesday.

Here’s Article 6, titled “Public Statements": “The NFLPA and the Management Council agree that each will use reasonable efforts to curtail public comments by Club personnel or players which express criticism of any club, its coach, or its operation and policy, or which tend to cast discredit upon a Club, a player, or any other person involved in the operation of a Club, the NFL, the Management Council, or the NFLPA.”

That’s the same clause that fueled the NFL’s attack against the NFL Players Association’s report cards. The process constitutes comments from the NFLPA that express criticism of the teams, their coaches, the operations, and their policies.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have ruled no one out for Thursday night. The Kansas Chiefs, on the other hand, will be without two starters and a defensive depth piece come Thanksgiving night. While the Bills haven’t made any official decisions on who is – or more accurately, who is not – playing tomorrow, they do have some question marks at key positions. There aren’t any surprises, however, on the week’s final injury report. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2125660875080274406?a=8WkBYLt6AG8DoW14dd0&s=20] What we’re thinking Dalton Kincaid will be a true game time decision. A stiff ankle in the cold, or more importantly slippery wet conditions, can be concerning, but it’s something they will likely keep testing right up until 6:50 when they have to make those inactive announcements. Dorian Williams and Christian Benford, on the other hand, are more likely to be game day decisions. Soft tissue injuries aren’t fun. Rest heals them, but cold temperatures can make those muscles tense up, and cause less-than stellar play at best with a setback in recovery a likely scenario. sports.body: What do I think is the biggest — and most specific — defensive key for the Buffalo Bills against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night? I’ll provide some metrics, and you’ll be able to reach the answer. The Chiefs are: * First in screen-pass rate in the NFL entering this game at 16.4% * Third in RPO rate at 8.4% and Patrick Mahomes has the: * Third-lowest average depth of target (aDOT) at 6.6 yards among 38 qualifiers * Fourth-quickest average time to attempt at 2.51 seconds among those same qualifiers * Fourth-lowest percentage of throws made 20-plus yards downfield at 9.2% among 33 qualifiers * Second-highest adjusted completion percentage at 81.1% You guessed it — tackling. The Chiefs, more than any other offense, put their opponents’ tackling capabilities to the test. How well have the Bills tackled this season, you ask? Below is a graphic that demonstrates the total amount of missed tackles credited to Bills defenders in each game by Pro Football Focus to date this season: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/correct-bills-missed-tckles-thru-wk11-1.png?quality=90&strip=all] After the bye week, which coincides with when CJ Gardner-Johnson was no longer on the team, the Bills have averaged six missed tackles per contest. In the six contests before the bye, Buffalo was averaging 8.5 missed tackles per game. Remember, before the spitting incident in Las Vegas, Gardner-Johnson was the owner of the highest missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties in the NFL. And don’t forget, on August 11, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said the following during a press conference on this very topic: > “Who can finish, get guys on the ground? That was an Achilles’ heel here last year. So that’s the No. 1 thing we have to correct.” Per PFF, in the regular season, the Bills averaged 8.88 missed tackles per game during the 2025 campaign. In Buffalo’s two playoff outings last season, that figure jumped to 9.5 per. Right now, even with the noticeably bad start, Buffalo’s missed tackles per game average is down to 7.5. And another strong showing in the tackling department for the Bills will go a long way in securing a win over the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, securing a 26-9 divisional victory at Highmark Stadium before turning their attention to a Thanksgiving night matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Buffalo out gained Miami 405-185, controlled the football for 36:45 and held the Dolphins to just two third down conversions on 14 attempts. Perhaps most impressive was the defense’s ability to keep Miami out of the end zone for all four quarters. There was plenty to celebrate in Buffalo’s locker room following Sunday’s victory, including a new career high for one defensive standout and another historic accomplishment for the Bills’ running back. Let’s take a look at who received game balls from head coach Joe Brady before handing out a few of our own. EDGE Greg Rousseau “Look, I could give this to everyone on defense the way y’all are playing right now,” Brady said before awarding his first game ball to Greg Rousseau. And rightfully so. Buffalo’s defense held Miami to just 185 total yards, 10 first downs and three field goals. But Rousseau finished the afternoon with three solo tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and two quarterback hits, accounting for both of Buffalo’s sacks and costing the Dolphins a combined 16 yards. His first sack came on Miami’s opening offensive possession when he brought down quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight yard loss on third and six, forcing the Dolphins to punt. With his two sack performance, Rousseau reached 10 sacks on the season, establishing a new career high with six regular season games still to play. Perhaps equally impressive is that Rousseau accomplished all of this while playing just 34 defensive snaps. RB James Cook Brady’s second game ball went to James Cook, who continues to rewrite the NFL record books. Cook finished Sunday’s contest with 22 carries for 89 yards and a touchdown. According to Brady, Cook became the first player in NFL history to record at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games. Brady also recognized Cook for reaching 1,000 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive season. And there’s still plenty of football left to be played. What continues to impress me about Cook is his consistency. sports.body: Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since 2025. Late on Tuesday, November 24 NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed “The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.” [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125442796467417433] “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career,” Pelissero added. Now feels like a perfect time to look back and judge whether the Jets made the right decision. In 2025 the Jets finished with a 3-14 record and Justin Fields delivered an uneven season before getting benched. He started nine games, completed 62.7% of his passes, threw for 1,259 passing yards, and had seven touchdowns to one interception. He also toted the rock 71 times for 383 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Pittsburgh had a 10-7 record in 2025 and made a trip to the playoffs, but ended up losing in the wildcard round. Aaron Rodgers started 16 games last season. He completed 65.7% of his passes, threw for 3,322 passing yards and had a 24 touchdown to seven interception ratio. It seems pretty obvious that Rodgers would have been a dramatic upgrade over what the Jets trotted out at QB last year. Things in 2026 feel quite the opposite. Before Rodgers got benched he started 10 games this year. He completed 60.9% of his passes, threw for 2,241 passing yards, and had a 16 touchdown to six interception ratio. The Jets are getting much better QB play than that with Geno Smith at the helm. Smith has started all 11 games so far this season. He has completed 68.1% of his passes, has thrown for 2,402 passing yards, and has a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. Seems like the Jets are better off with Smith in 2026 than Rodgers.
